heroSub: 10 Prachinburi stays we've reviewed in depth — a minimalist-design hotel in town, quiet garden resorts, a cacao farm stay near the waterfall side of Khao Yai, a wake-park resort on a lakeside, and a small garden B&B near the southern Khao Yai gate. Prices from about ฿400–2,000/night.
heroStats: ✅ Honest take from real reviews for every one
introH2: 🏙️ How many kinds of stays does Prachinburi have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Prachinburi is a province a lot of people overlook, even though it actually has more styles of accommodation than you'd think, and that's exactly what makes choosing a place here fun — some are minimalist-design hotels in town within walking distance of the night market and the public park, some are quiet garden resorts where you park right in front of your room, some are working farms where you get to make chocolate from cacao beans by hand, and some are small garden B&Bs near the southern Khao Yai gate that's quieter than the Pak Chong side. Plenty of people come to Prachinburi to run errands, to visit a patient at Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital, or to use it as a base before heading up Khao Yai on this side, then pick a stay that doesn't match their goal and end up feeling it wasn't worth it. This article rounds up 10 hotels and resorts in Prachinburi we've already reviewed in depth — in town, on the garden-and-foothill side, and on the Khao Yai waterfall side. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, with both the upsides and the honest caveats, a 3-site price compare, and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Prachinburi has no electric train, and many stays are out of town or down side lanes, so it's easiest when you drive yourself. From Bangkok it's about 130–150 km, roughly 2 hours, mostly on the motorway and then into Prachinburi. There are trains and vans/coaches into town too, but connecting onward within the province isn't as convenient as in a big city. The accommodation areas in this article: in town (Na Mueang, Tha Ngam, Khlong Kacha) — walk to the markets and the public park, near Abhaibhubejhr Hospital, good for errands. Suburbs and gardens (Mai Khet, Dong Khi Lek, Noen Hom) — quiet, garden atmosphere, good for driving in to unwind. Highway-side and the Khao Yai side (Ban Phra, Route 304, Khok Mai Lai, Prachantakham) — use as a base before heading up to the waterfall side and the southern side of Khao Yai.

entries.name: IRabbit Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Mueang · Walk to the market and public park
entries.addr: 54 Chaeng Phatthana Road, Na Mueang Subdistrict, Mueang Prachinburi District
entries.storyHtml: If we're going to start all 10 stays with the one that Prachinburi travelers talk about most often, plenty of voices give it to IRabbit Hotel — a minimalist-design 3-star hotel on Chaeng Phatthana Road in Na Mueang Subdistrict, opened in 2017 with 59 rooms, scoring 9.1 from 26 reviews on Trip.com, which counts as high for a small hotel in a secondary town. What makes people choose it is the central location where you can actually walk to food — about 590 m from the hotel to the night market, about 550 m to Prachinwanaram Public Park, and about 470 m to the provincial stadium. Around it are convenience stores and local eateries within walking distance, so in the evening you don't have to drive far. Rooms range from Standard Twin at about 24 sq.m. and Standard King with a large bed, up to Deluxe and family rooms. Every room has air-con, a flat-screen TV, a fridge and a minibar, and some have a balcony. What real reviews praise most consistently is that the rooms are clean, look new, and feel simpler and more modern than the older hotels in town, the beds are comfortable, and the bathrooms have hot water and a hairdryer, with the cleanliness score reaching 9.2 on Trip.com. There's free on-site parking, a 24-hour counter, CCTV, an elevator, and a bike-rental service so you can ride around town. Some guests even mention a resident hotel cat named "Oe" as a mascot to say hello to. Getting further out is convenient too: about a 15-minute drive to Abhaibhubejhr Hospital and the Thai Traditional Medicine Museum, with Khao Yai on the Prachin side not far beyond. Honest caveats from the reviews: the price is a touch higher than plain hotels in the province, with one review headlined bluntly "new, stylish, good service, a bit pricey," they take a deposit of about 500 baht at check-in that's refunded at check-out, rooms facing Chaeng Phatthana Road may hear some traffic, and because it's an in-town hotel there's no pool or spa. If you're here for errands, official business, to deal with Abhaibhubejhr, or for a single overnight on the way to Khao Yai and Kabin Buri, and you value cleanliness and a room that feels new, this is the most well-rounded option in town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want a quiet night, ask for a room not facing Chaeng Phatthana Road · have a deposit of about 500 baht ready at check-in · and don't miss walking over for good food at the night market, which is only about 600 m away.
pros: Clean rooms, look new, minimalist design more modern than older hotels in town
Central location, walk to the night market and public park
Free parking, 24-hour counter, bike rental available (from the reviews)
Score 9.1 from 26 reviews, heavily weighted on cleanliness and service
cons: Price a touch higher than plain hotels in the province
A deposit of about 500 baht is taken at check-in
It's an in-town hotel, with no pool or spa

entries.name: Greenfield Residence
entries.addr: 98 Tha Ngam Subdistrict, Mueang Prachinburi District
entries.storyHtml: If IRabbit is the central-town side, Greenfield Residence is the quiet side that budget travelers and people visiting a patient talk about — a 3-star residence-style stay of about 32 rooms down a lane in Tha Ngam Subdistrict, scoring 7.9 from 12 reviews on Trip.com. Its number-one selling point is the quiet and a location where it's just about a 5-minute drive to Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital and Wat Kaeo Phichit, an old temple with mixed Thai-Chinese-European architecture that's a landmark of the province. The stay sits about 200 m down a lane off the main road, so it's noticeably quieter than hotels right on the main road, with the town center, markets and public park about a 10-minute drive away. Rooms split into Standard and Deluxe, with the Deluxe at about 20 sq.m. on floors 1–2, available with either a queen bed or two single beds. Every room has air-con, a fridge, a flat-screen TV with cable channels, a hairdryer, and a private balcony looking out over the garden, a spot many people like to sit and sip coffee in the morning. What real reviews praise most consistently is that the rooms are clean with no musty smell, the floors are glossy, the bed and pillows are comfortable, and the quiet suits a full night's sleep — many sum it up simply as "good value, clean, quiet." There's free parking, a 24-hour counter, CCTV, a snack bar with room service, and laundry service. Honest caveats from the reviews: the stay is down a lane, so it suits people with a car more than those using public transport; first-timers may find the lane a little hard to find and should pin the map; parking is limited when it's busy; breakfast costs extra and is a simple affair; and it's an in-town residence with no pool or spa. It suits best people with their own car, those visiting a patient at Abhaibhubejhr, those running errands in town, or anyone wanting a quiet stay with clean rooms on a high-hundreds budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Enter the coordinates and pin the map before you set off, because the stay is about 200 m down a lane from the main road · if you care about the view and quiet, ask for an upper-floor room or one facing the garden · and if you're visiting a patient at Abhaibhubejhr, choosing this saves a lot of back-and-forth time.
pros: Quiet down a lane, good for relaxing and a full night's sleep
5-minute drive to Abhaibhubejhr and Wat Kaeo Phichit
Clean rooms, no musty smell, private garden-view balcony (from the reviews)
Budget-friendly price, free parking, 24-hour counter
cons: Down a lane, suits people with their own car more
Parking is limited when busy · breakfast costs extra
It's an in-town residence, with no pool or spa

entries.name: Aroonsawad Riverview Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Decha · About 15 min from town
entries.addr: 81 Moo 3, Bang Decha Subdistrict, Mueang Prachinburi District
entries.storyHtml: Aroonsawad Riverview Resort sits on a balance that isn't easy to find — quiet by the river yet still about a 15-minute drive into town. It's a small riverside resort of about 16–19 rooms in Bang Decha Subdistrict, Mueang District, in a modern-vintage green-toned style, scoring 7.2 on Trip.com and 3.6 out of 5 on TripAdvisor (ranked #7 of 15 specialty-lodging stays in the province). Picture waking up in the morning, opening your bungalow door, and a few steps later you're on the walkway along the Prachinburi River, watching the water drift by under a thin mist before going down for a soak in the garden pool. Rooms split into two groups — single-story Deluxe bungalows in the garden with air-con, a fridge, a flat-screen TV and a kettle, and two-bedroom, two-bathroom villas with a living room and a small kitchen, good for families or groups of friends, some facing the river for a full water view. The highlight is the outdoor pool ringed by trees and the riverside walkway that's prettiest in the morning and evening. There's a riverside restaurant, a cafe, free parking, and a seminar room for about 60 people. Real reviews praise the quiet riverside atmosphere and the friendly staff — even lower-scoring reviews still acknowledge the good service. Honest caveats: the stay is down a riverside village lane that public transport can't reach, there are no eateries to walk to nearby, you need a car and have to drive into town for food, the counter isn't open 24 hours so you should call ahead, and the room standard isn't consistent across every unit, with some reviews grumbling that certain rooms are getting old, so ask to see the room at check-in. It suits best couples, families, and anyone wanting a quiet riverside atmosphere while still being near town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Confirm your booking and ask about directions ahead of time at 037-287112 or 084-661-2200, because the location can be hard to find and the counter isn't open 24 hours · if you want a full water view, specify a room or villa facing the river · and ask to see the room at check-in because the room standard isn't consistent.
pros: Quiet riverside atmosphere, with a garden pool and a riverside walkway
Near town, about a 15-minute drive in
Two-bedroom villa is good value for families or groups
Staff are friendly and helpful (from the reviews)
cons: Down a riverside lane, no eateries to walk to nearby, you need a car
Room standard isn't consistent, some rooms are getting old (from the reviews)
Counter isn't open 24 hours, you should call ahead

entries.name: Deva Garden Resort
entries.badge: 🌿 Garden resort · Park at your door
entries.addr: 32 Moo 11, Mai Khet Subdistrict, Mueang Prachinburi District
entries.storyHtml: Among these 10 stays, if you measure it by "what you get per baht spent," Deva Garden Resort is the one many people say is more than worth it — a small garden resort of about 7 rooms in Mai Khet Subdistrict, Mueang District, with real reviews in good shape at about 8.1–8.6 (Agoda 8.6) and prices from just about ฿552/night, which counts as one of the lightest in this set. The standout is that the rooms sit in a shady garden — every room has a garden-view balcony that opens onto greenery, good for sitting with a morning coffee. Most rooms are king-size, with air-con many reviews praise as nice and cold, a flat-screen TV, a work desk, and an en-suite bathroom with a hot shower, and some rooms have an added terrace. What real reviews praise over and over is the free private parking right at your room door — convenient, safe, no dragging your bags far — plus the quiet and privacy from having few rooms, so there's little noise from neighbors, and the kind owner who looks after guests like family that comes up often. The Mai Khet area is near Rajabhat/Ramkhamhaeng University's Prachinburi campus, about 1.2 km away, and the government district, so it's convenient for people running errands, visiting students, or stopping over before exploring the Khao Yai–Khao Ito side. From Bangkok it's about 130–150 km. Honest caveats from the reviews: there's no pool and no breakfast included, no full on-site restaurant (but you can order delivery), not many eateries directly within walking distance, and it's in an area where public transport isn't convenient, so it suits people who drive themselves best. With only about 7 rooms, it fills up fast over long weekends. If your goal is a clean, quiet sleep with easy parking at a light price, this does it all.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Since breakfast isn't included and there's no on-site restaurant, plan your meals ahead — order delivery, bring food in the car, or drive into town · the stay has about 7 rooms and fills up fast over long weekends, so book ahead · and if you arrive late, contact the owner in advance because there's no 24-hour front desk.
pros: Clean rooms, cold air-con, quiet, shady garden atmosphere (from the reviews)
Park at your room door, convenient and safe
Owner and staff are friendly and kind
From about ฿552, good value for running errands in town
cons: No pool and no breakfast included
Not many eateries within walking distance, you rely on a car or delivery
Only about 7 rooms, fills up fast over long weekends

entries.name: Panpim Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Dong Khi Lek-Noen Hom · Near durian orchards
entries.addr: 93/1 Moo 8, Ban Nong Chuang, Dong Khi Lek Subdistrict, Mueang Prachinburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you're tired of tower hotels where every room is identical and you want a stay that's a little cottage in a green garden where you wake to birdsong, Panpim Resort is what many people are after — a small garden resort of about 9–10 cottages in the Noen Hom-Dong Khi Lek area, Mueang District, that's owner-run, scoring 8.6 from 83 reviews on Trip.com. The cottages are bungalow-style, spread through the garden, with large shade trees, lawns, and garden-side sitting corners. Every room has a balcony or terrace opening onto the garden, and inside there's air-con, a fridge, a TV, a hot-water bathroom, and Wi-Fi that reviews rate very highly. What gets praised most consistently is the owner who looks after guests like welcoming a friend home — foreign reviews call them "the cutest couple ever," with the service category climbing to about 9.4 — and the fresh-made Thai breakfast included in the room rate, which many say is one of the highlights of the stay. There's a shady green garden, a BBQ corner for grilling your own, bikes to borrow, a lawn for kids to play, and free parking. As a base for exploring around Prachinburi it's easy: about 15–20 minutes to town and Abhaibhubejhr, about 10–15 minutes to Khao Ito Waterfall and Chakrabongse Camp, and about 115–136 km from Bangkok. Honest caveats from the reviews: the location all but requires a car — there are no shops to walk to nearby, little public transport, and renting a motorbike is hard; there's no pool; some rooms have a slight musty smell when the air-con is first turned on that usually clears with ventilation; and there's the owner's dog barking at times. It suits best couples, small families, and nature-leaning travelers who drive in to unwind quietly.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Don't miss the fresh-made Thai breakfast already included in the rate, eaten garden-side in the morning to birdsong · if you're sensitive to smells, ask to air out the room before checking in · and plan ahead for dinner because there are no eateries to walk to nearby — buy something to grill at the BBQ corner or drive into town.
pros: Quiet garden atmosphere, bungalows set in the garden, private
Owner-run and lovely like family, service score about 9.4 (from the reviews)
Fresh-made Thai breakfast included in the room rate
Clean rooms, good Wi-Fi, from about ฿700, good value
cons: You need a car, no shops to walk to nearby, renting a motorbike is hard
No pool, few amenities given the size
Some rooms have a musty smell when the air-con is first on · owner's dog barks at times

entries.name: Saengcha Farm Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Prachantakham · Near the waterfall side of Khao Yai
tags: 🌿 Near the waterfall side of Khao Yai
entries.addr: 104/2 Moo 7, Pho Ngam Subdistrict, Prachantakham District, Prachinburi
entries.storyHtml: If you want a Prachinburi stay that isn't an in-town hotel but a genuine working farm where you get to make chocolate from the bean by hand, Saengcha Farm Resort is the stay foreign travelers talk about a lot — a family farm stay in Pho Ngam Subdistrict, Prachantakham District, on the waterfall zone of the Khao Yai side, scoring 9.2 from 9 reviews on Trip.com. What sets it apart from other stays is that it's an agricultural farm that's still actually working, not a resort that landscapes a garden to look like a farm. This land grows cacao (cocoa) and agarwood, with a small on-site facility making bean-to-bar chocolate and agarwood oil, run by an owner named Munin and siblings who look after guests at every step themselves. The highlight is the chocolate workshop using cacao beans they grow themselves (open about 9:00–16:00, booking ahead recommended). The owners walk you through the plots, explaining everything from planting, harvesting the pods, fermenting, drying, roasting and grinding to molding, then let you make it yourself, with several recipes to taste and buy to take home. The drinks reviews mention over and over are the coffee and the Mexican Chocolate. The rooms are several styles of garden bungalow, with the barn-shaped Barn House having a high, airy ceiling, and reviews praise the rooms as clean, warm and well-equipped. Breakfast is included, the owner's brother cooks it himself with a vegetarian option using vegetables from the farm plots, and the owner even takes guests for a walk with the farm's six dogs in the evening. The location is near Heo Narok and Than Thip waterfalls, about 15 minutes from Prachantakham town and about 40 minutes from Prachinburi town. Honest caveats from the reviews: the location is remote, with no shops to walk to nearby, easiest when you drive yourself (the farm offers pickup-drop-off from Bangkok and the train station for a fee), there's no pool, and everything must be booked ahead because it's a family farm with limited staff. It suits best people who want an experience more than a bedroom.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Contact the owner ahead via Line/WhatsApp to book the chocolate workshop and ask about the home-cooked meals, because everything is prepared to the number of guests · if you're not driving, ask about the farm's pickup-drop-off service in advance · and leave room to visit the Khao Yai-side waterfalls the same day because the location is right near the waterfall zone.
pros: Chocolate workshop from cacao they grow themselves, you can't find this elsewhere
Owner looks after guests personally, warm like staying at a friend's
Home-cooked food is tasty, with a vegetarian option (from the reviews)
Clean rooms, high airy ceilings, near the waterfall side of Khao Yai
cons: Remote location, no shops to walk to nearby, you need a car or the pickup service
No pool, a simple farm stay focused on the experience
It's a small stay, meals and activities must be booked ahead

entries.name: Wannida Garden Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ban Phra · Near Ban Phra junction, Route 304
entries.addr: 9/9 Moo 8, Ban Phra Subdistrict, Mueang Prachinburi District
entries.storyHtml: Among these 10 stays, if you measure it by the lightest starting price, Wannida Garden Resort is the one starting at about ฿400/night, alongside Baanmaichaiklong — a budget-friendly garden-bungalow stay of about 28–32 rooms in Ban Phra Subdistrict, Mueang District, near Ban Phra junction and Suwannason Road (Highway 304) in the 304 Industrial Estate zone, with an overall Agoda score of about 6.0 from about 213 real reviews (TripAdvisor 2.4/5 from a small number of reviews). Picture driving Route 304 from Bangkok heading to Khao Yai or in for business at the estate, and when you're tired you pull off for a simple place where you can park right at your room. An easy reference point is across from the Dynasty-Thai Top tile center, near the Mitsubishi center, about 200 m from the traffic-light junction. The rooms are standalone single-story bungalows lined up in a garden, surrounded by trees, giving more privacy than rooms in a row block, and you can park near your room. They split into Standard with a queen bed and Deluxe with a king bed, and inside there's air-con, a water heater, a TV and free Wi-Fi. On the okay side, reviews say some units are clean with fresh towels changed daily, the air-con is cold and the hot water works, the Wi-Fi is fast enough, and there's a 24-hour reception that can take drivers arriving late. Honest caveats from the reviews: the most-mentioned thing is that the room standard isn't consistent — some rooms have hard or broken beds, damaged furniture, and some lack a fridge or a bin, so ask to see the room and check the air-con, hot water and bed at check-in, then take photos. The location is in the estate/highway zone, with no eateries to walk to nearby, so you need a car and should bring food. There's no pool, it's a non-smoking stay, and pets aren't accepted. It suits best drivers who want a budget overnight near Highway 304, or people on business in the estate area, who aren't fussed about luxury.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Confirm the price and directions ahead at 037-216839 or 084-103-7444, because the info on each booking site doesn't always match · since the room standard isn't consistent, ask to see the room and check the air-con, hot water and bed at check-in · and bring food in the car, especially if you arrive late, because food is hard to find around the stay.
pros: From about ฿400/night, one of the lightest in this set
Rooms are standalone garden bungalows, convenient parking at your door
Cold air-con, working hot water, free Wi-Fi, 24-hour reception
Highway-side location is easy to find, near Ban Phra junction and Route 304
cons: Room standard isn't consistent, some rooms have hard beds or incomplete fittings (from the reviews)
In the estate/highway zone, no eateries to walk to nearby
No pool, no pets, it's a non-smoking stay

entries.name: Baanmaichaiklong Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khlong Kacha · Near town and Abhaibhubejhr
entries.addr: 49/8 Moo 1, Suwinthawong Road, Khlong Kacha Subdistrict, Mueang Prachinburi District
entries.storyHtml: Picture sleeping in a raised wooden house with a breeze passing underneath, opening the window to a still canal in the morning, and the only sounds you hear are the wind and the birds — Baanmaichaiklong Resort is a small wooden-house resort of about 16 rooms in Khlong Kacha Subdistrict, Mueang District, that chose to sell simplicity and canalside quiet over luxury. It's a 3-star stay at about Agoda 7.0 with prices from just about ฿400/night. The rooms are raised wooden houses, the signature in its name, split into about 8 Standard rooms (from about ฿400) and about 6 Deluxe rooms (about ฿600–800), simply decorated with a TV, a water heater and Wi-Fi. Some rooms are air-con and some are fan, depending on the price tier, so check clearly when booking. The charm of a raised wooden house is the airy feel, the breeze passing through, the sense of staying at an upcountry garden home. Real reviews agree the place is "a relaxed riverside atmosphere, quiet, no noisy crowds of tourists, with lovely friendly service." The location is in Mueang District, so it's not a far drive into town, near Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital, V.N.D Golf Course and the Prachinburi tennis courts, which is very useful for people on business or visiting relatives at the hospital. There's parking, laundry service, and a massage service. Honest caveats from the reviews: this is a folk wooden house in the low hundreds, with simple rooms that aren't brand new, and some rooms may be old with the age of the wood. There's no pool or large on-site restaurant, online reviews are still few (on Trip.com it still shows as awaiting reviews), you should have your own car because it's down a lane that may be hard to find, and pets aren't accepted. It suits best budget travelers who want a quiet sleep by the canal within Prachinburi town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Book directly and ask the stay directly at 037-211545 or 086-111-1888, because online reviews are still few and the info on booking sites may be incomplete · ask clearly whether the room you book is air-con or fan · and ask to see the room at check-in because some rooms may be old with the age of the wood.
pros: From about ฿400, good value for a stay in town
Raised-wooden-house canalside atmosphere, quiet, not crowded (from the reviews)
Friendly service like a small owner-run stay
In town, near Abhaibhubejhr and food spots · massage service available
cons: Simple rooms, some may be old with the age of the wood, ask to see the room first
No pool or large on-site restaurant · online reviews are still few
You should have a car, it's down a lane that may be hard to find · no pets

entries.type: Resort + Wake Park on a Lakeside
entries.name: Atlantis Extreme Park
entries.badge: 🏄 Wakeboarding on-site · On the Khao Yai route
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khok Mai Lai · On the Khao Yai/Na Di route
entries.addr: 198/10 Moo 7, Suwannason Road, Khok Mai Lai Subdistrict, Mueang Prachinburi District
entries.storyHtml: Where the other stays in this set sell quiet and cleanliness, Atlantis Extreme Park chose the opposite — an activity-filled getaway. It's a small outdoor-activity-style resort in Khok Mai Lai Subdistrict, on the out-of-town Prachinburi side toward Khao Yai/Na Di, that blends the stay with a wakeboarding ground (Wake Park) all in one place, scoring 8.6 on Trip.com, though from a small sample, so read it as a guide. Picture waking up in the morning, walking out of your room, and there's a wide private lake with a cable strung across it to pull wakeboards. The number-one highlight is the private lake fitted with a cable system to pull wakeboards, which you can ride without a tow boat, good for practice from beginner level, and in the same lake you can also kayak and swim. On land there's a gym and an outdoor Muay Thai ring, and on the relaxing side there's a Thai herbal steam sauna and an aroma massage room to ease your muscles after a full day. There's a fitness room, a barbecue service, a bar, and free parking. The restaurant serves a distinctive menu of Spanish food (paella, churros), Italian and Western that several reviews say tastes better than expected. And pets are welcome to stay at no extra charge, which is rare. Every room is a lake-view room with air-con, a flat-screen TV, a fridge and a kettle, and it works easily as a base for Khao Yai and the Nakhon Nayok waterfalls since it's about a 15–20 minute drive. Honest caveats from the reviews: there are very few rooms (about 5–7 rooms/suites), hard to book at peak, and the system notes extra beds aren't possible; there's no breakfast included in the rate; the shared facilities are limited; online reviews are still thin; and it's an out-of-town stay that needs your own car, with wakeboarding and gear-rental fees possibly charged separately, so ask first. It suits best groups of friends, active couples, and families who like outdoor activities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask clearly whether the wakeboarding and gear-rental fees are included in the room rate or charged separately, plus the daily ride times · since online reviews are still few, message the Atlantis Wake Park page to confirm it's open, the current prices and room availability · and plan your own breakfast because the room rate doesn't include it.
pros: Lake for wakeboarding and kayaking on-site, this kind of activity is hard to find in this area
Herbal steam sauna, massage room, and an outdoor Muay Thai gym
Spanish-Italian-Western food that tastes better than expected · pets welcome
Use as a base for Khao Yai and the Nakhon Nayok waterfalls, a 15–20 minute drive
cons: Very few rooms, hard to book over long weekends · no extra beds
No breakfast included in the rate · online reviews are still thin
Out of town, you need your own car · activity fees may be charged separately

entries.name: B&B Forest Hill Khao Yai
entries.badge: 🏡 Near the southern Khao Yai gate · High score
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Noen Hom · <2 km from the southern Khao Yai gate
entries.addr: 68 Moo 15, Noen Hom Subdistrict, Mueang Prachinburi District
entries.storyHtml: Closing out all 10 stays with one of the most consistently high-scoring in real reviews — B&B Forest Hill Khao Yai, a small Bed & Breakfast the owner runs at every step, located in Noen Hom Subdistrict, Mueang District, near the southern gate of Khao Yai National Park (the Prachinburi side), less than 2 km away, scoring 9.2 from 115 reviews on Booking.com. It has just 2 cabanas in a tropical garden, Elephant and Tiger, so it's very quiet and private, with only a few groups of guests each night. Picture waking up in the morning in a cabana in the middle of the garden, opening the balcony door to a backdrop of the Khao Yai range, and a few steps away is the pool where someone serves freshly-made breakfast poolside. The Elephant Cabana, 58 sq.m., has a king-size bed, a sofa-bed living corner that folds out for an extra bed, and a small kitchen with a fridge, sleeping 2–4, while the Tiger Cabana is the smaller one, good for 2. Both have a front balcony and a rooftop with a Khao Yai view that many say is most striking in the morning and evening. The highlights are the outdoor pool that looks onto the Khao Yai range, the tropical garden laid out into several tree zones, the outdoor kitchen with a BBQ stove, free bikes to borrow, and most praised of all, the fresh-made breakfast served by the pool — bacon, eggs, home-baked bread, seasonal fruit, coffee and tea — and the friendly owner with a warm welcome, which reviews describe as "like staying at a friend's house." This southern-gate location is quieter than the Pak Chong side that's lively every weekend. From Bangkok it's about 140 km, with town and Abhaibhubejhr about 20–30 minutes away. Honest caveats from the reviews: the location all but requires a car — there are no shops within walking distance and little public transport; with only 2 cabanas it fills up fast over holidays, so book ahead; it's a B&B with no all-day restaurant and no spa or fitness; and there's no 24-hour front desk, so everything must be arranged with the owner in advance. It suits best couples or two people who want the Prachinburi side of Khao Yai genuinely calm and private.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Book as early as possible because there are only 2 cabanas, and long weekends and the cool season fill up very fast · confirm breakfast and check-in time with the owner in advance because there's no 24-hour front desk · and if you're 3–4 people or want to cook your own food, choose the Elephant Cabana with the extra sofa bed and a small kitchen.
pros: Small owner-run B&B, friendly with a warm welcome (from the reviews)
Spacious cabanas, very clean, with a Khao Yai-view rooftop
Pool looking onto the Khao Yai range · fresh-made breakfast served by the pool
Less than 2 km from the southern Khao Yai gate, avoiding the Pak Chong crowds
cons: You need a car, no shops to walk to nearby, little public transport
Only 2 cabanas, fills up fast over holidays, you must book ahead
It's a B&B with no all-day restaurant, no spa/fitness

faqTitle: FAQ — Questions travelers often ask about staying in Prachinburi

faq.q: ❓ What's the best place to stay in Prachinburi?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style · if you measure by real review scores, Saengcha Farm Resort and B&B Forest Hill Khao Yai get about 9.2, the highest in this set · if you want to stay central and walk to the market, IRabbit Hotel scores 9.1 · if you want a good-value garden resort, Panpim Resort 8.6 or Deva Garden Resort 8.4 · if you want an activity trip, Atlantis Extreme Park has a wakeboarding lake on-site

faq.q: ❓ How much does a Prachinburi stay cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at about ฿400–2,000 per night · the lightest side is Wannida Garden Resort and Baanmaichaiklong Resort, from about ฿400, and Deva Garden Resort at ฿552 · the mid level is Greenfield ฿650, IRabbit and Panpim ฿700, Saengcha ฿850, Atlantis ฿900 · the higher level is Aroonsawad ฿1,500 and B&B Forest Hill ฿2,000 · all prices are approximate starting rates from the standard room, and over festival periods and the cool season on the Khao Yai side prices may be higher than usual

faq.q: ❓ Which area is good to stay in in Prachinburi?
faq.a: In town (Na Mueang, Tha Ngam, Khlong Kacha) suits people on errands, visiting a patient at Abhaibhubejhr, walking to markets and eateries (IRabbit, Greenfield, Baanmaichaiklong) · Suburbs and gardens (Mai Khet, Dong Khi Lek, Bang Decha) suit people driving in for a quiet rest (Deva Garden, Panpim, Aroonsawad) · The Khao Yai side and highway-side (Prachantakham, Khok Mai Lai, Noen Hom, Ban Phra) suit using as a base for Khao Yai and the waterfalls (Saengcha, Atlantis, Forest Hill, Wannida)

faq.q: ❓ Do you need a car for a Prachinburi stay?
faq.a: Mostly you should have your own car, especially the garden-side, Khao Yai-side and down-a-lane stays (Deva Garden, Panpim, Saengcha, Aroonsawad, Atlantis, Forest Hill, Baanmaichaiklong, Wannida), because there's usually no shop within walking distance and little public transport · if you don't have a car, an in-town stay like IRabbit Hotel is the most convenient to walk to markets and eateries · Saengcha Farm offers pickup-drop-off from Bangkok and the train station (for a fee) for people without a car

faq.q: ❓ Which Prachinburi stay is good as a base for Khao Yai?
faq.a: It depends on which side of Khao Yai you're entering · B&B Forest Hill Khao Yai is near the southern Khao Yai gate (the Prachinburi side), under 2 km, avoiding the Pak Chong crowds · Saengcha Farm Resort and Atlantis Extreme Park are on the waterfall/Na Di side, about a 15–20 minute drive to the waterfalls and the Khao Yai ascent · and Panpim Resort in the Noen Hom-Dong Khi Lek area also works as a base for getting out around the province

faq.q: ❓ Which Prachinburi stay has a pool?
faq.a: In this set, the ones with a pool are Aroonsawad Riverview Resort (a garden pool by the river) and B&B Forest Hill Khao Yai (a Khao Yai-view pool), while Atlantis Extreme Park has a lake for swimming and wakeboarding · the in-town stays and small garden resorts like IRabbit, Greenfield, Deva Garden, Panpim, Saengcha, Wannida and Baanmaichaiklong have no pool, because they focus on simplicity and a budget-friendly price
